Site.title: Site
Site.description: Represents a website created within Neup.Sites.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Site entity.

logoUrl.description: URL of the website's logo image.

hideSitename.description: Whether to hide the site name in the header, useful if the logo contains the name.

description.description: A short description of the site.

socialProfiles.description: A list of social media profiles.

contactPhone.description: A list of contact phone numbers.

status.description: The current status of the site (e.g., pending, active, inactive).

type.description: The type of website (e.g., real estate, news portal, academic institution, personal portfolio, corporate portfolio).

modules.description: A map of feature modules and their activation status for the site.

active.description: Whether the module is active for the site.

enabledOn.description: The date and time when the module was enabled.

expiresOn.description: The optional date and time when the module access expires.

Page.title: Page
Page.description: Represents a page within a website.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Page entity.

path.description: The URL path for the page (e.g., /onboarding).

content.description: The HTML content of the page.

requiresPendingSite.description: Whether this page requires the site to be in a pending state to be accessible.

Path.title: Path
Path.description: Represents a URL path that maps to a page.

siteId.description: The ID of the site this path belongs to.

pageId.description: The ID of the page this path maps to.

content.description: The main content of the article, likely in Markdown.

publishedAt.description: The date and time the article was published.

definition.description: Stores site information. The 'siteId' is the unique identifier for the site.

params.name: siteId
params.description: The unique identifier for the site.

definition.description: Stores page information associated with a specific site. The 'siteId' is the site's unique identifier, and 'pageId' is the page's unique identifier.

params.name: siteId
params.description: The unique identifier for the site.

params.name: pageId
params.description: The unique identifier for the page.

definition.description: Stores individual news articles. The document ID is a combination of a slug and a random ID.

params.name: newsId
params.description: The unique identifier for the news article.

definition.description: Stores URL path mappings to pages.

params.name: pathId
params.description: The unique identifier for the path mapping.

firestore.reasoning:
This design prioritizes security and scalability by adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, Access Modeling, and Data Clarity. 

The `sites` collection stores site data. The `pages` subcollection stores page data related to the site.

**Authorization Independence**: No `get()` calls are needed in the security rules because access control is based on the `status` field in the `sites` collection and `requiresPendingSite` field in the `pages` collection. All required attributes for pages authorization are denormalized into the page document itself, removing the need for hierarchical dependencies.

**Structural Segregation**: The `sites` collection is dedicated solely to site data, ensuring a homogeneous security posture. Similarly, the `pages` subcollection only contains page documents associated to a specific site.

**Access Modeling**: The structure uses path-based ownership (`/sites/{siteId}/pages/{pageId}`).

**QAPs**: The segregation of sites and pages based on the site ID supports efficient and secure list operations, as queries can be scoped to a specific site.

**Invariants**: The structure supports invariants by associating pages to sites via the `siteId` field in the `pages` subcollection. This ensures the integrity of the 1:N relationship between sites and pages.
